headerInfo.manblitz: Pressure with man behind it. Somebody comes free and everybody is covered.
headerInfo.zoneblitz: Pressure with zone behind it. Bring one, drop one, let the QB guess wrong.
headerInfo.matchcov: Match coverage. Zone eyes that turn into man the second the routes declare.
headerInfo.zonecov: Zone shells. Keep everything in front, rally and tackle, no free deep balls.

about.headline: BAMA MATCH PHILOSOPHY
copy: This is one piece of a much bigger defense we are building for College Football 27. We have already got the full 4-2-5 nickel installed, and this match coverage series is the layer that goes on top of it.
Quarters today, then Palms, then the rest of Saban's coverage family. And after that we have got the 3-4 and our nickel 3-3-5 stuff for the teams that want to line up heavy and try to run it on you.
If you want to see everything that is up so far, the playlist is linked below.

principles.title: MATCH IS AGGRESSIVE ZONE WITH RULES
principles.blurb: Not passive zone, not pure man. Zone defenders reading routes and reacting to whatever they get.
principles.detail: So what actually is match coverage. It is not passive zone and it is not pure man, it is zone defenders reading routes after the snap and reacting to whatever they get. A guy can lock somebody up in man and take him away completely, or he can come off and go double team somebody else, or he can just sit there looking for work and help on anyone who shows up in his area. And that is what makes it so hard to throw against, because the picture the quarterback read before the snap is not the picture he is throwing into.

principles.title: MATCH KILLS THE META ROUTES
principles.blurb: Corners, crossers, deep posts. Quarters takes away every route people are living on right now.
principles.detail: Here is why this matters right now. All the routes people are abusing online, the corners, the crossers, the deep posts, quarters takes every one of them away. Our corners are playing man on demand so nothing gets in behind them, our safeties are reading and closing on anything vertical, and you end up with double teams sitting right at the catch point on the exact throws that usually beat you. And all of it comes out of a two high shell that tells the offense absolutely nothing before the snap.

principles.title: WHY SABAN BUILT HIS DEFENSE ON MATCH
principles.blurb: One defense with an answer for everything. Spread, empty, heavy. The rules adapt.
principles.detail: What match coverage gave Saban was one defense with an answer for everything. It does not matter if they come out spread, or empty, or heavy with two tight ends, the rules adapt to whatever formation and routes they give you, so he was never guessing and never rebuilding his scheme week to week. That is how he stayed the best defense in the country for seventeen years while offenses changed completely around him. And the way he played it, he could sit in a two high shell all game and still contain the run.

playbook.title: RUN THE VIRGINIA PLAYBOOK
playbook.note: In game, this whole defense runs out of the VIRGINIA playbook. Every front and every call on the sheet lives inside it. In Ultimate Team the same defensive playbook shows up under four other names, so any of these five gets you the exact same book.

about.rulesNote: These are the rules for match coverage, not a formation. They travel: any scheme, any defense you are running can play them, and the numbering never changes. The 4-2-5 under this is just where we line up.

jobs: THE NOSE AND BOTH ENDS IN THE 34 ODD.
THE TWO DTS WHEN WE SLIDE TO NICKEL.
EAT THE DOUBLE TEAMS SO THE BACKERS RUN FREE.
HOLD THE POINT AND SET THE TONE INSIDE.
BLOW UP RUNS BEFORE THEY EVER GET STARTED.
PUSH THE POCKET WHEN WE ONLY RUSH FOUR.
THE OUTSIDE BACKERS IN THE 34 ODD.
THE B ENDS WHEN WE GO BIG NICKEL.
FREE RUNS AT THE QUARTERBACK OFF THE EDGE.
WIN THE ONE ON ONE WHEN THEY DO GET BLOCKED.
GET HOME RUSHING FOUR, NO HELP NEEDED.
DROP INTO COVERAGE JUST OFTEN ENOUGH TO LIE.
THE TWO INSIDE BACKERS IN EVERY PACKAGE.
THE GREEN DOT. THEY RUN THE WHOLE SHOW.
BIG AND FAST IS THE JOB DESCRIPTION.
RANGE TO COVER SIDELINE TO SIDELINE.
FIRE DOWNHILL WHEN THE BLITZ IS CALLED.
CLOSING SPEED THAT FINISHES AT THE QUARTERBACK.
THE MATCH COVERAGE ANCHORS OUTSIDE.
PRESS THE LINE AND CARRY EVERY VERTICAL.
ON AN ISLAND WITH NO HELP OVER THE TOP.
SIZE TO WIN THE JUMP BALLS OUTSIDE.
ZONE EYES THAT SNAP TO MAN WHEN ROUTES DECLARE.
NEVER OUT OF PHASE, NEVER PANICKED.
THE BACK END THAT MAKES EVERY DISGUISE WORK.
TWO DEEP AT THE SNAP, ANYWHERE AFTER IT.
ROTATE LATE SO THE QUARTERBACK READS LIES.
THE STAR NICKEL COMES OUT OF THIS ROOM.
SPEED AND RANGE TO ERASE THE DEEP BALL.
THE LAST LINE. NOTHING GETS BEHIND US.

pillars.name: The Rules
pillars.eyebrow: the count, and who has who
pillars.line: Quarters against a plain 2x2, which is where the numbering lives. One is the outside receiver, two is the next man in. The corner plays man on demand, the safety reads two to one, and everything after this is the same rules against a harder picture.

checks: The corner takes #1 unless #2 releases outside
The safety carries #2 vertical and robs him if he breaks in
It is a match, never a spot drop

pillars.name: The Formations
pillars.eyebrow: when they compress, go trips, or go empty
pillars.line: Bunch stops the count working, so the rule changes to quadrants: first one deep and outside, first one deep and inside, first one shallow. Trips gets Palms. Empty is just 3x2, two sets of rules on one call, with the corner sitting on number two to the flat instead of bailing.

checks: Against bunch you match the quadrant, not the number
Palms keeps a free man on the back end against trips
Empty splits into a trips side and a two side

plays.name: Cover 4 Quarters vs 2x2

reads.label: CB · Outside Corner
reads.text: #1 goes vertical (5+ yards) and he locks him up in man. #1 breaks in or shallow and he zones off, looking to help on #2. If #2 runs a corner or a streak he doubles him. Both stay short and he sinks back into the deep quarter.

reads.label: FS · Safety
reads.text: #2 goes vertical and the safety plays him man. Streaks, corners, posts. #2 breaks in or shallow and he scans to #1 to bracket anything deep. Both stay shallow and he is free help over the middle, doubling crossers from the other side.

reads.label: SS · Safety
reads.text: #2 goes vertical and the safety plays him man. Streaks, corners, posts. #2 breaks in or shallow and he scans to #1 to bracket anything deep. Both stay shallow and he is free help over the middle, doubling crossers from the other side.

reads.label: CB · Outside Corner
reads.text: #1 goes vertical (5+ yards) and he locks him up in man. #1 breaks in or shallow and he zones off, looking to help on #2. If #2 runs a corner or a streak he doubles him. Both stay short and he sinks back into the deep quarter.

reads.label: QF · Quarter Flat
reads.text: Cap #2 if he releases vertical, then get eyes to the flat and take anything out there. #2 goes flat right away and he covers him. #2 runs a wheel and he matches it upfield, converting to man. No flat threat and he buzzes under any dig or curl behind him. On a drag: away from the back he carries it across. On the back's side he passes it to the 3 Rec Hook.

reads.label: QF · Quarter Flat
reads.text: Cap #2 if he releases vertical, then get eyes to the flat and take anything out there. #2 goes flat right away and he covers him. #2 runs a wheel and he matches it upfield, converting to man. No flat threat and he buzzes under any dig or curl behind him. On a drag: away from the back he carries it across. On the back's side he passes it to the 3 Rec Hook.

reads.label: 3 REC · 3 Receiver Hook
reads.text: In 2x2 he is mostly free, with no locked in man assignment. His job is to help over the middle and pick up crossers or late flat routes. He takes the second player to the flat: once the quarter flat gets run off, the next one out there is his. A floater. He doubles crossers, jumps underneath routes and cleans up the space the quarter flat cannot reach.

adjustments: #1 is the outside receiver.
#2 is the next man in, slot or tight end.
#3 only shows up on trips.
Reads run outside in.

plays.name: Cover 4 Palms vs 3x1

reads.label: CB · Trips Corner
reads.text: MEG on #1. Man everywhere he goes, no exceptions. Vertical, inside, across the field, it does not matter. He travels. No switching and no passing off. This is pure man.

reads.label: QF · Nickel / Apex
reads.text: #3 goes fast to the flat (arrow, whip, quick out) and he takes him right away, matching him to the flat and running with him. #3 goes vertical or into the middle (5 yards or more, seam or crosser) and he snaps his eyes to #2 and mans him up. Once he is on #2 he takes him anywhere on the field, short or deep.

reads.label: FS · Trips Safety
reads.text: #3 goes vertical and the safety takes him. Seam, post, corner, anything vertical. #3 stays shallow and #2 goes vertical and he picks up #2 and takes him wherever he goes. Both #2 and #3 stay shallow and he is free help over the top, usually doubling #1 on a post or a deep dig.

reads.label: 3 REC · Mike
reads.text: First rule: wall off #3 if he goes vertical or crosses. Stay underneath him until the safety takes it, then drift back into space. If the back is already taken by the apex and somebody else comes into that flat late, the Mike picks him up. Otherwise he sits in the middle, reads the quarterback and looks for crossers and digs.

reads.label: QF · Solo Apex
reads.text: He has the running back. Swing, angle or wheel, it is man everywhere he goes. If the back stays in to block he sits in the flat, watches for late releases and drives on checkdowns.

reads.label: SS · Solo Safety
reads.text: This is the free player. He is your robber and he can help anywhere. #1 on his side goes vertical and he brackets him with the corner. #1 breaks inside or shallow and he looks back across the field to help on crossers from the trips side. That back side help on crossers and deep digs is what makes Palms elite.

reads.label: CB · Solo Corner
reads.text: MEG on #1. Man everywhere he goes. If the solo side is an inline tight end instead of a receiver: vertical or a corner route and he takes him man. If that tight end breaks inside, the safety takes him across and this corner looks for work from the trips side.

adjustments: #1 is always the outside receiver.
#2 is the next man in, slot or tight end.
#3 is the inside most man in the trips.
Everything counts outside in.
Takes away the corner routes and flood concepts trips lives on.
You still get a free robber on the back side.
Two high shell, so it gives up nothing pre snap.
Still fits the run with the safeties.
